Peromyscus leucopus is the primary reservoir host for Borrelia burgdorferi in the northeastern and mid-Atlantic U.S., including Maryland.

Studies show that white-footed mouse densities can reach 20–80 individuals per hectare in suitable habitats (deciduous forests, edge environments, suburban woodlots), with peak densities during late summer and fall.
Using the 30% forest/suburban land cover assumption again for Maryland (~720,000 hectares), and assuming a moderate reservoir density of 50 mice per hectare, we get:
